Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 51, verses 1–4:

The waw here is the waw of oath (wāw al-qasam). These are oaths by which the Real (al-Ḥaqq), glory be to Him, swears. We do not swear except by Allah, because the believer has no greatness above the greatness of Allah. As for al-Ḥaqq, glory be to Him, He swears by whatever He wills of His creation, because He, glory be to Him, knows best the aspects of greatness in them and the places of wisdom in each oath among them.

For example, He, glory be to Him, swears saying: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it covers over﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 1-2]. Why did He, glory be to Him, swear specifically by the morning brightness and by the night when it covers over, and not by anything else?

This oath came in response to the disbelievers of Makkah when revelation paused from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They rejoiced and said: "The Lord of Muḥammad has forsaken him."

So the oath here has a purpose and a fitting connection. The morning (ḍuḥā) is the place of movement and work, and the night is the place of rest and stillness, and each of them does not do without the other.

Here is an indication of the wisdom behind the pause of revelation. It is as if He is saying to them: reflect on the time that encompasses you, and how it is night for rest and day for work, and each of them completes the other.

Likewise, the matter of revelation: when it first descended upon the Messenger of Allah, it was difficult for him and exhausting to him (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) described this hardship, saying concerning the angel... So the pause of revelation from the Messenger of Allah was an opportunity in which he rested from the toil and longed to meet the angel anew. Thus he likened the first descent of revelation to the day and its pause to the night.

Here al-Ḥaqq, glory be to Him, swears by the adh-Dhāriyāt, which are the winds. Winds are a force and energy necessary for life in this universe. ﴿Scattering (dharwan)﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 1], meaning they scatter things and set them in motion. The adh-Dhāriyāt are those that carry water vapour to the places where clouds form.

Then He said after them: ﴿Then those that bear heavy loads﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 2], and these are the clouds, which carry water and gather until they become heavy, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Do you not see that Allah drives the clouds, then joins them together, then makes them into a heap, and you see the rain coming out from their midst…﴾ [al-Nūr: 43].

Al-wiqr means a heavy burden. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And He produces the heavy clouds﴾ [al-Ra'd: 12]. Then these clouds, after they are formed, do not stand still in their place; rather the winds move them.

﴿Then those that run with ease﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 3], meaning the clouds move with a light motion and glide through the space with lightness and softness.

As for His saying: ﴿Then those that distribute the command﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 4], meaning those that distribute these clouds and drive them to the places where they fall, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿He strikes with it whom He wills and turns it away from whom He wills…﴾ [al-Nūr: 43]. Then comes the answer to these four oaths:

﴿Indeed, what you are promised…﴾.

The Qur'an verse is: "By the sky with its pathways" (Surah al-Dhariyat 51:7) — not included here. Here is the translation of the passage as given:

Its meaning: what you are promised of resurrection and reckoning is ﴿true indeed..﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 5], a reality that will certainly occur, and ﴿the Judgment is surely going to occur﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 6]. "The Judgment" means the Day of Judgment, the Day of recompense for deeds, ﴿surely going to occur﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 6], taking place and happening without any doubt.

But what is the connection between swearing by these things and the truth of the Day of Judgment?

They said: when you look at the universe in which we live, you find that the Creator, glorified is He, created everything in it, and all these elements are as they are in God's universe since God created them, and they will remain until the Day of Resurrection, such that only the human being will be brought back into creation.

Take, for example, water or air, by which God swore. You find that water is itself since God created this universe; it neither increases nor decreases, because it circulates in a cycle that returns it to the natural water which God created.

So you, for example, drink in the journey of life several tons of water, for instance. Does it remain in you? No, it leaves you in the form of urine, sweat and the like, and returns again to its source. Thus, even the small amount that remains in the human body is absorbed by the earth after his death and returns to the groundwater.

So here is an indication that you are born, die, return, and We bring you back again. Take from the material universe around you a proof of the possibility of your being returned again; take the material and observable as evidence of the truth of the unseen which God has informed you of. So do not consider it unlikely that what perishes returns again.

This is another oath by which Allah, glorified is He, swears by the heaven: ﴿by the heaven full of paths﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 7]. It comes from the root (ḥ-b-k), and we say, for example: this thing is ḥubbik (finely wrought), meaning it has been made with precision, with neither excess nor deficiency. Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 51, verses 10-14:

The meaning of ﴿الْخَرَّاصُونَ﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 10] is "the liars," as He said in another verse: ﴿They are only conjecturing﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 20]. But how can He say ﴿Killed are...﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 10] when they are alive? They said: the intended meaning here is that they have been cursed by Me and banished from My mercy. Killing removes you from the bounties of this world, whereas cursing removes you from the mercy of Allah in the Hereafter and places you in His punishment, and we seek refuge in Allah.

It is as if He, glorified is He, is saying to them: Whom do you kill and whom do you curse? Rather, it is you who will be killed, resurrected and called to account, and it is you who will be cursed and driven away from the mercy of Allah.

Then He describes them, glorified is He, with His saying: ﴿who are in heedlessness, unaware﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 11]. They say: "ghamarahu al-ma'" means that the water covered him and drowned him. So it is as if ignorance has submerged these people until they drowned in it and it blinded them. The meaning of ﴿sahun﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 11] is: heedless, careless, turned away from what is intended for them.

Such people have no salvation on the Day of Resurrection, the day they deny and ask about with the question of doubt and mockery: ﴿When is the Day of Recompense?﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 12], meaning: when is this day?

So Allah explains it to them: ﴿the Day they will be tested over the Fire﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 13]. The Day of Recompense that you deny is this day on which you will be cast into Hell and will taste punishment in its various forms, as the reward for your mockery and derision.

﴿Taste your trial...﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 14]: taste the effects of your trial in this world. The Fire is also called "fitnah" (trial, testing) when it smelts metal, for example, in order to purify it and expel its impurities.

So the Day of Recompense about which you ask with mockery and denial is the day on which you will be tested over the Fire and burned by it, just as gold and iron are tested. Although gold and iron are tested so that their dross and impurities are removed and they become solid, you are tested over the Fire so that you will be punished by it and endure pains that never end.

﴿This is it﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 14], meaning: the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, ﴿that which you used to hasten﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 14]. Their hastening for it is the result of their denial of it; had they believed that it is true, they would not have hastened for it.

The Qur'an has recorded their saying: ﴿So bring us what you promise us, if you are among the truthful﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 22].

Thus: their question about the Day of Recompense, ﴿When is the Day of Recompense?﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 12], is mockery of it and denial of it, because they believe in an unseen matter that Allah has informed about, while they have taken the material blessings that Allah has bestowed upon them, and by which He created benefit for them. Yet they took the blessing and did not turn to the Bestower; rather they were deceived by the blessing and said what they said of denial and mockery.

Therefore we find many verses that argue with them by proof and evidence, and establish for them that the Resurrection is true. When they said: ﴿Shall we, when we are bones and dust, be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ [Al-Isra: 49], He answered them: ﴿Say: Be stones or iron, or a creation of what is great in your breasts. They will say, "Who will restore us?" Say, "He who created you the first time..."﴾ [Al-Isra: 50-51].

Because they considered the revival of bones far-fetched, He moved them to a state beyond bones, for bones have a basis in life. So He says to them: even if you were inanimate, stones or iron, which are characterized by hardness and have no connection with life, We are capable of reviving you.

After the Truth, glorified is He, spoke about those who obstinately opposed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and denied the Resurrection, He mentions the opposite, and we have said that mentioning the opposite clarifies the picture, and the opposite shows the beauty of its opposite. So He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 51, verses 15–19:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous (al-muttaqin)...﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 15]. "Inna" (indeed) serves to emphasize the statement. "Al-muttaqin" is the plural of "al-muttaqi." And taqwa, as we have said, is that you place between yourself and the punishment of Allah a shield (wiqayah). Therefore we find the Qur'an saying once: ﴿And fear Allah...﴾ [al-Hashr: 18], and once it says: ﴿And fear the Fire...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 131].

The meaning is: adhere to the obedience of Allah, and avoid His disobedience and the causes of His punishment. For Allah, the Exalted, has attributes of beauty (jamal) and attributes of majesty (jalal), and taqwa is that you place between yourself and the attributes of majesty a shield against the attributes of majesty, which restrain the transgressor and turn him back from evil.

Among the attributes of beauty is that He created for us what we benefit from in this world, and among that is the Fire: ﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle? Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 71–72].

But this fire, from which you benefit in this world and which is counted as one of the blessings of Allah upon you, beware of it in the Hereafter, for it will be an instrument of punishment; it will be one of the soldiers of Allah for subduing the disobedient. So fear it. Therefore the meaning is one: fear Allah, and fear the Fire.

You will also notice here that ﴿al-muttaqin﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 15] is in the time of obligation (taklif), and it is plural, and ﴿jannat﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 15] is in the time of recompense, and it is plural; and likewise ﴿wa 'uyun﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 15]. It is as if the Exalted Truth is saying: indeed for every God-fearing person there is a garden and springs flowing through it—yes, a garden specific to him, because the rule is that when a plural is matched with a plural, it requires distribution into singulars.

Just as a teacher says to his pupils: "Take out your books," meaning that each of them should take out his book. But in Surat ar-Rahman He, glorified be He, says: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ [ar-Rahman: 46].

How do we reconcile and harmonize the two verses? They said: because in Surat ar-Rahman the address is to the two weighty groups, jinn and humankind; so the meaning is: and for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, whether of mankind or jinn, a garden—a garden for mankind and a garden for jinn.

Or the meaning is: he has two gardens in actuality. We have already explained that Allah created the Garden on the assumption that all of humanity would believe, and created the Fire likewise, sufficient for all of humanity if they do not believe.

We said: there is no housing crisis there. When the people of the Fire enter the Fire, their places in the Garden become vacant, and the righteous inherit them. So it is as if he takes his garden and the garden of the disbeliever who abandoned it and went to the Fire.

The garden (jannah) is an orchard full of trees with intertwined branches, such that it shelters the one who walks in it and conceals him; or it means that in it are all the necessities of life, such that one does not need to leave it—just as we say of the word qasr (palace): your palace is in its place away from other places, so you do not leave it for another place to seek the means of life.

He said: ﴿in gardens and springs﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 15], i.e., springs of water, because gardens are essentially characterized by greenery, growth and fruits, and such things come into being through the existence of water. So the springs in the gardens are for their sustenance and permanence as a garden.

Therefore, when the Noble Qur'an spoke of the rivers of the Garden and the provision of the water necessary for them, it said once: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ [at-Tawbah: 100], and once said: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ [as-Saff: 12] (the latter with "min" before "tahtiha").

From here it indicates that the water is inherent within it, lest we think that the flowing water that passes by it may cease, so that someone says to you: rest assured, for the water of the Garden is guaranteed because it springs from within it.

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿taking what their Lord has given them﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 16]. The context here returns to the past tense and speaks to us of the reason: these righteous ones attained this recompense because they took the method of Allah with contentment and acceptance.

﴿Akhidhin﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 16] is the plural of the active participle "akhidh," which is one who takes a thing with longing and eagerness, and takes it with contentment and acceptance. A person does not extend his hand to take except for something beneficial to him, unlike a thing thrown at you which you take while unwilling.

It is as if these people heard the method of Allah, and knew that in it lay the sustenance of their lives, the protection of their conduct, and the salvation of their Hereafter, so they took it—they took it with eagerness, love and longing; they took it with strength, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Take what We have given you with strength﴾ [al-Baqarah: 63].

The strength in taking indicates that the taker values the beautiful benefit he attains. Then, you took and others left; you did well and they did evil, although you are free and have absolute liberty to take or to leave.

You have done well while being able to do good and able to accept evil. Your hearing the revelation of Allah, obeying, and bearing the obligations with contentment and acceptance—this makes you worthy of this recompense.

Then the verses show that the taking here is a restricted taking: we do not take everything and whatever comes to us, but rather we take what has come to us from our Lord and Creator: ﴿taking what their Lord has given them﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 16]. He chose here the attribute of lordship (rububiyyah) because it is a giving: the Lord is the One who created from non-existence and provided from nothingness, and by His self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah) preserved for you the necessities of life. We say: so-and-so is qa'im 'ala al-amr, meaning he is concerned with it and does not leave it to others.

So Allah, by His wisdom and power, created; and by His self-subsistence, He sustains the good. Therefore, whenever good comes to you, remember the lordship that bestowed it upon you. And lordship is prior in human life to divinity (uluhiyyah), for Allah gave you and provided for you before you were created, and did not obligate you except after reaching puberty.

Since you have taken the gift of lordship and enjoyed it, it becomes incumbent upon you to take the gift of divinity. Just as you took the first gift with love, desire and longing, so you must take the other gift also with love, desire and longing. It is not becoming of you to take the first and leave the second and disown it, for if you reflected on the gift of divinity you would find it more beneficial to you than the gift of lordship, and more lasting.

The first gift of lordship gave you the necessities of the worldly life, which are temporary and perishing; it gave you the necessities of the vanishing shell (qalib). But the gift of divinity is a gift that guarantees you the enduring Hereafter and quickens in you the enduring spirit which does not perish. So: which of the two is more deserving of being taken?

Therefore, when the Exalted Truth spoke to us about this matter, He said: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to conceal your private parts, and as adornment; but the clothing of righteousness—that is best﴾ [al-A'raf: 26].

So the clothing that covers the private parts represents the necessities, and the feathers (rish) are for adornment and luxuries, and this is the utmost we take in this world. Then He draws attention to what is more important: ﴿but the clothing of righteousness—that is best﴾ [al-A'raf: 26], better than the bliss of this world, its adornment and its ornaments, because this is passing and that is lasting and enduring. The clothing of this world covers you in this world, while the clothing of taqwa covers you in this world and in the Hereafter.

And since the gift of divinity has this importance, Allah has not given it except to one who believes in Him by choice; therefore only the believer is obligated. That is why we always read in the context of obligations: ﴿O you who have believed...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 153].

Then the verses mention another attribute of the righteous: ﴿Indeed, they were before that doers of good﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 16], i.e., they did not merit this station except because they ﴿were before that doers of good﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 16]. Ihsan (excellence) is a high degree of faith, which the scholars defined, saying: ihsan is what came in the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: and ihsan is the increase in acts of obedience beyond what Allah has commanded you. Therefore this verse was revealed in Makkah before zakah was prescribed in Makkah. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and in their wealth is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 19], and did not say "a known right." The known right is zakah, which was prescribed in Madinah, whereas charity (sadaqah) existed in the Makkan period.

So the meaning of ihsan is that they proceeded to the levels of ihsan before being obligated to them, which means that the levels of ihsan are innate and natural, within your capacity, and do not burden you; and likewise all matters of obedience and steadfastness come naturally without effort, in contrast to disobedience.

Therefore we say: the steadfast person, for example, saves the cost of sitting in cafes, smoking tobacco, coffee, narcotics and intoxicants. Steadfastness, economically, is more profitable for its possessor.

Even in the action of the limbs, steadfastness comes naturally, whereas disobedience requires effort, sneaking and deceit. Therefore, in linguistic derivation, the Qur'an expressed obedience with (kasaba) and disobedience with (iktasaba).

Acquisition (kasb) is a natural matter, and "kasaba" is on the pattern fa'ala; whereas "iktasaba" contains ifti'al and is on the pattern if'tala. You see this ifti'al in one who schemes to look at what Allah has forbidden him, how he sneaks and steals glances from people; you also see it in one who goes to the mosque and one who goes to the tavern, and so on.

The scholars have defined the degree of ihsan in worship, saying: ihsan is that you perform what Allah has obligated upon you of worship, and add to it of the same kind as what Allah has obligated; so the believer performs the five prayers, and the one who does ihsan performs them and adds to them what he can of voluntary prayers.

The believer pays zakah at the rate of one-half of a tenth or one-quarter of a tenth, and the one who does ihsan pays beyond that, and so on.

So the muhsin here has two meanings: that he did good before the obligation and hastened to good deeds before they were imposed upon him; or that he performed what was obligated upon him and then added beyond what was obligated of the same kind.

Then the Exalted Truth describes the doers of good saying: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 17]. Hujuw' (sleeping) is: remaining still from movement in good and not doing evil. We say to a mischievous child whose movement increases: ihja' (be still), meaning: cease the disturbing movement.

From here they said: the sleep of the wrongdoer is worship—yes, worship, because it restrains him from wrongdoing. These people may pray the 'isha' and sleep after it until dawn; but their love of obedience made them sleep only a little of the night, and negating sleep is, a fortiori, negating slumber.

Ihsan is the result of the servant's love for his Lord. Allah did good to you when He obligated you and greeted you with this obligation, so you should return the greeting with something better: if He obligated you to five prayers, make them ten; if He obligated you to one-half of a tenth or one-quarter of a tenth in zakah, make it many times that; and so on in all acts of worship and avenues of good.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about ihsan, he said: that you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you. Imagine that you are a hired worker with a man who sits behind you, watching you and observing all your movements: could you then be negligent in your work or fall short in it?

Likewise is the state of the muhsin in his worship, and it has come in the hadith qudsi: ...

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿and at the dawns they seek forgiveness﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 18]. Al-asḥar is the plural of as-saḥar, which is the last part of the night before the break of dawn, when a faint light appears that makes a person imagine it is sunlight though the sun has not yet risen; hence it is called imaginary light.

From the same root is the word sihr (magic), for magic is the reversal of realities through imagination, having no reality. From it is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people...﴾ [al-A'raf: 116].

And since the gift of divinity has this importance, Allah has not given it except to one who believes in Him by choice; therefore only the believer is obligated. That is why we always read in the context of obligations: ﴿O you who have believed...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 153].

Then the verses mention another attribute of the righteous: ﴿Indeed, they were before that doers of good﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 16], i.e., they did not merit this station except because they ﴿were before that doers of good﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 16]. Ihsan (excellence) is a high degree of faith, which the scholars defined, saying: ihsan is what came in the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: and ihsan is the increase in acts of obedience beyond what Allah has commanded you. Therefore this verse was revealed in Makkah before zakah was prescribed in Makkah. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and in their wealth is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 19], and did not say "a known right." The known right is zakah, which was prescribed in Madinah, whereas charity (sadaqah) existed in the Makkan period.

So the meaning of ihsan is that they proceeded to the levels of ihsan before being obligated to them, which means that the levels of ihsan are innate and natural, within your capacity, and do not burden you; and likewise all matters of obedience and steadfastness come naturally without effort, in contrast to disobedience.

Therefore we say: the steadfast person, for example, saves the cost of sitting in cafes, smoking tobacco, coffee, narcotics and intoxicants. Steadfastness, economically, is more profitable for its possessor.

Even in the action of the limbs, steadfastness comes naturally, whereas disobedience requires effort, sneaking and deceit. Therefore, in linguistic derivation, the Qur'an expressed obedience with (kasaba) and disobedience with (iktasaba).

Acquisition (kasb) is a natural matter, and "kasaba" is on the pattern fa'ala; whereas "iktasaba" contains ifti'al and is on the pattern if'tala. You see this ifti'al in one who schemes to look at what Allah has forbidden him, how he sneaks and steals glances from people; you also see it in one who goes to the mosque and one who goes to the tavern, and so on.

The scholars have defined the degree of ihsan in worship, saying: ihsan is that you perform what Allah has obligated upon you of worship, and add to it of the same kind as what Allah has obligated; so the believer performs the five prayers, and the one who does ihsan performs them and adds to them what he can of voluntary prayers.

The believer pays zakah at the rate of one-half of a tenth or one-quarter of a tenth, and the one who does ihsan pays beyond that, and so on.

So the muhsin here has two meanings: that he did good before the obligation and hastened to good deeds before they were imposed upon him; or that he performed what was obligated upon him and then added beyond what was obligated of the same kind.

Then the Exalted Truth describes the doers of good saying: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 17]. Hujuw' (sleeping) is: remaining still from movement in good and not doing evil. We say to a mischievous child whose movement increases: ihja' (be still), meaning: cease the disturbing movement.

From here they said: the sleep of the wrongdoer is worship—yes, worship, because it restrains him from wrongdoing. These people may pray the 'isha' and sleep after it until dawn; but their love of obedience made them sleep only a little of the night, and negating sleep is, a fortiori, negating slumber.

Ihsan is the result of the servant's love for his Lord. Allah did good to you when He obligated you and greeted you with this obligation, so you should return the greeting with something better: if He obligated you to five prayers, make them ten; if He obligated you to one-half of a tenth or one-quarter of a tenth in zakah, make it many times that; and so on in all acts of worship and avenues of good.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about ihsan, he said: that you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you. Imagine that you are a hired worker with a man who sits behind you, watching you and observing all your movements: could you then be negligent in your work or fall short in it?

Likewise is the state of the muhsin in his worship, and it has come in the hadith qudsi: ...

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿and at the dawns they seek forgiveness﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 18]. Al-asḥar is the plural of as-saḥar, which is the last part of the night before the break of dawn, when a faint light appears that makes a person imagine it is sunlight though the sun has not yet risen; hence it is called imaginary light.

From the same root is the word sihr (magic), for magic is the reversal of realities through imagination, having no reality. From it is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people...﴾ [al-A'raf: 116].

The time of saḥar is among the best times for seeking forgiveness. But for what do these people seek forgiveness, whom their Lord described as God-fearing, who took what their Lord gave them, attained the degree of ihsan, and used to sleep little of the night?

So: they have no sins to seek forgiveness for. It has been said: these people have a form of seeking forgiveness befitting the degree of ihsan; they do not seek forgiveness from their sins, but rather they seek it for the shortcoming they imagine in their worship and deeds, as if they regard what they have done as insufficient compared with what Allah deserves of glorification and worship. This is of the category of "the good deeds of the righteous are the sins of those brought near."

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿and in their wealth is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 19]. He attributed the wealth to them, saying ﴿their wealth﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 19], because they now possess it, although in reality it is the wealth of Allah, and man is a steward over it for a time.

Therefore He, glorified be He, said: ﴿and spend of that in which He has made you successors﴾ [al-Hadid: 7].

Man is the vicegerent of Allah on earth, and he is obligated, by the requirement of this vicegerency, to obey the command of the One who appointed him to give to the beggar and the deprived from the wealth of Allah deposited with him: giving to the one incapable of work and earning, even giving him in gratitude to Allah who granted him the strength to work, while others are incapable and deprived of that strength.

When the Exalted Truth commands us to this, He is in fact securing the life and future of both the capable and the incapable of work, because time turns over people, and the events of life are constantly changing; perhaps the one capable today will be incapable tomorrow, and then he will find someone extending a hand of help to him.

Therefore we have said: the wise Lawgiver taught us to work according to our capacity, not according to our need. When you work according to the capacity which Allah placed in you, you will take your need and give charity to one who is unable to work; and if this solidarity and this insurance were available to us, man would live without fearing the events of life and without dreading poverty for himself and his descendants after him.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 19]: the beggar (sa'il) is the needy one whom need compels to ask people; likewise the deprived (mahrum) is also needy, but he abstains from asking, and so he is deprived and perhaps goes hungry or perishes; in this case he is sinful against his own self, because Allah has prescribed for him to ask. He is deprived of ownership first, and he deprived himself second of the asking that was prescribed for him.

From here Islam urged acquaintance and attendance at gatherings in which people become acquainted and ask about one another; through this acquaintance we know the needy and help them, and we know the sick and visit them, and so on.

A certain righteous man was approached by a beggar, and he gave him what he needed. Then his wife entered upon him and found him weeping, and she said to him: What makes you weep, when you have given him what he needed? He said: I weep because I left him until he had to ask me.

Therefore, the obligation is that the right reaches its owners without asking: it is an obligation upon the wealthy to spare the poor the humiliation of asking.

The earth is the earth on which we live, and it is singular in form, but in reality there are multiple lands, as the Exalted said: ﴿He created seven heavens, and of the earth [He created] the like of them...﴾ [al-Talaq: 12]. Thus there are seven earths.

They said: because the earth comprises multiple environments in terms of climate, heat and cold, and in terms of soil, what it contains of elements, and what it brings forth of goods. From here the lands have multiplied. Therefore the scientists say: this is the wheat belt, for example, and this is the banana belt, and this is such-and-such belt.

So the Truth, glory be to Him, gave each land what suits it for a specific plant that fits the inhabitants of it. The fault is that we transfer the produce of one land to another land that is not suitable for it; and if it were suitable for the inhabitants here, it would be found among them.

Therefore we find that a plant outside its land is afflicted by blights. If we look, for example, at the banana belt, you find it strong in its places, not struck by any blight or ruin; but if you transplant it to a land other than its own, blights multiply on it and ruin befalls it.

It is as if the Creator, glory be to Him, is saying to us: this was not created for your environment; rather it has its environment in which it flourishes, where the requisites of its growth are available.

The āyāt (ʾāyāt, plural of āyah) are the signs indicating the power of the Creator, glory be to Him. The first of the signs in the earth we observe in the distribution of the surface of the earth between water and dry land. Water is of two kinds: sweet, palatable (ʿadhb furāt), and salty, bitter (milh ujāj).

From the sweet we drink, and we water the crops and the animals; and from the salty we take fish: ﴿and from each you eat fresh flesh and extract ornaments that you wear...﴾ [Fatir: 12].

The earth contains fertile, easy land suitable for cultivation, and it contains deserts and mountains, and in each are the goods that suit it. Among the signs in the earth is that water covers three-quarters of the dry land, and the wisdom in that is that the expanse of water widens, and the expanse of evaporation widens, which then gives us the rain that suffices for drinking and for cultivation.

So: salt water is the reservoir of water on the earth, and God made it salty to preserve it from ruin and protect it from change. The Exalted says: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, until when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land, and We send down water therewith, and bring forth thereby all kinds of fruits. Thus do We bring forth the dead; perhaps you will remember.﴾ [al-A'raf: 57].

Among the signs in the earth is that the courses of sweet waters are at a higher level than the courses of salt waters; and if the salt were higher, it would corrupt the sweet waters and we would not benefit from them. The Exalted says: ﴿Between them is a barrier they do not transgress.﴾ [al-Rahman: 20].

Among the wonders of power in the creation of plants is that you find the finest kinds of date palms and figs, for example, on salt shores, as in al-ʿArish and elsewhere; and this is from the freedom of power that is not bound by causes, but does what it wills. So from salt water we eat the most delicious and sweetest fruits.

Among the signs in the earth are the mountains: ﴿And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of varying hues, and jet black.﴾ [Fatir: 27]. The mountains, as we have said, are reservoirs of fertility, reservoirs of sustenance, and reservoirs of many goods of minerals and precious stones.

We have previously explained that the Truth, glory be to Him, scattered the goods and distributed them over the whole earth, such that if we took from the earth a section from its surface to its center, we would find in it goods equal to the other section: this has minerals, this has petroleum, this has crops, and so on.

Among the signs in the earth is that you find the soil one and watered with one water, yet it yields different fruits and different tastes: ﴿And in the earth are neighboring plots, and gardens of grapes, and crops, and palm trees, some multiple-stemmed and some single-stemmed, watered with one water; yet We make some of them excel others in fruit. Surely in that are signs for a people who understand.﴾ [al-Ra'd: 4].

Yes, they understand the power of God in creation, and that these signs were created by a Powerful, Wise, Self-Subsisting One.

Here He said: ﴿Signs are in the earth for those who have certainty﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 20], i.e., those who are certain of that and believe in it. The highest degree of knowledge is the cosmic sciences that investigate the universe and derive from its signs the power of God.

Read, for example: ﴿Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colors? And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of varying hues, and jet black. And among mankind and the beasts and cattle are those of varying colors. Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear God...﴾ [Fatir: 27-28].

Note that He did not mention here any legal ruling concerning fasting, prayer, or zakat. Therefore, the "scholars" here means the scholars of nature and the cosmos, who investigate plants, animals, humans and inanimate matter, and who infer the Powerful from power, and lead people to the court of faith in the Creator; and this is a truth that benefits them in this world and the next.

One who reflects on the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And in the earth are signs for those who have certainty﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 20] understands from it that a person who looks at the universe around him and infers from it the existence of the Creator, glory be to Him. Therefore He put the disbelievers in a trap when He asked them: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say: God...﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87], and ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say: God...﴾ [al-Zumar: 38].

Yes, they said nothing else, because it is a matter as clear as the sun, and no one claimed it for himself. And how could he claim it, when he was created an infant unable to do anything? How could he say "I created myself," when he came upon the universe as it is? How could he claim that he created it?

As for the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And in yourselves; will you not then see?﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 21], i.e., just as there are cosmic signs in the earth indicating God's power, so there are signs in yourselves. If you do not reach the signs of the universe around you, then look into yourself, which is between your two sides.

The Exalted said: ﴿Will you not see?﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 21] because the signs of the universe around you, if they are far from you, the signs of yourself are near you, and more worthy of observation and reflection.

The signs in the self are many. Take, for example, the body's temperature: you find it one and the same, 37°, for one living at the frozen pole and for one living at the equator; and the movement of the organs and limbs is not sound except at this degree; and if it increased, the whole system of the body would be disordered and its movement would be disturbed.

Within the body, each of its systems has a temperature suited to it without any heat transfer occurring within the single body, as we know. If the general temperature of the body is 37°, the temperature of the eye, for example, stops at nine degrees and does not exceed them; and if it exceeded that, the eye would burst.

As for the liver, it does not perform its function in the body except at forty degrees; and the wonder is that this difference is within one skin and one body. Blessed is God, the best of creators.

Likewise, if you reflect on the blood that flows in the veins, the breath, the heart, the brain, the bones, everything in your body contains a sign, indeed signs; when you contemplate them you say: Glory be to the Creator, the Originator, glory be to Him who possesses the freedom of power.

So: there is no argument for one who has not believed after seeing the signs in himself and in the universe around him.

This style is called in rhetoric (balagha) the style of restriction (qasr), by placing the prepositional phrase before the subject: sustenance is in the heaven only, not in anything else. Your provision comes to you from above, from God. And sustenance (rizq) is everything that one benefits from: wealth is sustenance, health and well-being are sustenance, reason is sustenance, and security is sustenance.

As for the meaning of "sustenance is in the heaven," it means that it is a matter and an eternal decree written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). If you mean the material life we live, its source is also the water descending from the sky, for it is the foundation of life and the source of nourishment.

﴿And what you are promised﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 22], meaning: it is also in the heaven. Everything is predetermined and written in the Preserved Tablet, every small and great thing, whatever departs and whatever arrives. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but it is in a clear register﴾ [al-An'am: 59].

Therefore: since provisions are apportioned by God, and since everything is written from eternity, then be graceful in seeking, and do not preoccupy yourselves with the matter of provision, except that you go to it and strive in seeking it. You do not create it, but you go to it, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿So walk through its regions and eat of His provision...﴾ [al-Mulk: 15].

So walking and striving is a cause (sabab) for the provision apportioned to you from eternity. We have learned this lesson from Sayyidah Hajar, the mother of Isma'il, when Sayyidina Ibrahim left her, along with her son, at the Ka'bah and departed, and she said: "Did God command you to do this?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Then He will not neglect us."

She was certain that provision is with God. Her running seven rounds between as-Safa and al-Marwah was but a model of striving. It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, wanted to make her a witness to the truth of this verse. When Sayyidah Hajar had exhausted her means in striving, she returned to her child, reassured by her saying: "Indeed God will not neglect us."

At that moment the child struck the earth with his foot, and Zamzam gushed forth from beneath it. After that, God made it one of the rites (mash'ar) of Hajj and 'Umrah so that it would always remind us of this truth: that provision is with God, but seeking it is required, and movement in its direction is one of its causes.

Al-Asma'i related that one day he met a Bedouin. The Bedouin asked him: "Where are you from?" He said: "From Asma'," (a place name). He said: "Where have you come from?" He said: "From the mosque." He said: "And what do you do there?" He said: "We recite the Book of God." He said: "Then recite to me."

So I recited to him Surah adh-Dhariyat until I reached His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision, and what you are promised﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 22]. The Bedouin then brought the hunting tools he had with him and broke them, and said: "As long as my provision is in the heaven, by God, He does not lie."

Al-Asma'i said: I went out with Harun al-Rashid for the Hajj, and I met this Bedouin again, but this time he was thin and yellow of complexion. I said to him: "Are you not so-and-so?" He said: "Are you not al-Asma'i?" I said: "Yes. What has reduced you to this?"

He said: "Recite to me what you recited before." So I recited to him until His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is indeed the truth, just as it is true that you speak﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 23]. He marvelled and said: "Who angered the Majestic One so that He was compelled to swear an oath?" He kept repeating it, and before he had finished the third repetition his soul departed with it.

It was also related to me once that I was performing the Hajj together with Shaykh Ahmad Abu Shuqqa, and it occurred to us to climb up to the Cave of Hira. He said to me: "We need a guide to direct us." I said: "We know the way," and we set off. But we found that they had broken the path leading to the cave, and we lost our way.

Then my companion withdrew from me to one side to urinate, and suddenly he said to me: "Look, Shaykh!" I looked, and behold, an insect had come and began drinking from his urine. I said: "Glory be to God! It seems we lost the way so that we could give this insect a drink." Then a man passed by us who knew that we had lost the way, and he guided us.

Here the Almighty, exalted is He, swears by His own Essence, and by His lordship over the heaven and the earth, because from the heaven rain descends, and the earth receives this rain and grows by it the plants on which the sustenance and life depend.

As for His saying: ﴿It is indeed the truth..﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 23], that is, His saying: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision, and what you are promised﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 22], this is a true statement without doubt, because it is an eternal decree recorded in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

Then He gives us an example that makes this matter concrete, saying: ﴿just as it is true that you speak﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 23]. Just as you know that you are speaking, and just as you are certain of this reality and have no doubt about it because you experience it yourself, so too do not doubt the matter of provision, that it is from God, and trust this report, because the One who informed you of it is truthful.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 51, verses 24–25:

This is an information from Allah, exalted is He, about our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Because it is an important and wondrous report, the Truthful One (al-Haqq, subhanahu) began it with this interrogative: ﴿Has there come to you...﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 24]. Is it always the case that a wondrous thing, which deserves our attention, is introduced by such an interrogative?

Allah, exalted is He, makes us eager to know it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ [al-Saff: 10]. He makes us eager, so that we say: "Yes, O Lord, guide us."

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 51 (al-Dhariyat), verses 31–34:

﴿He said...﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 31] That is, our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said to the people who entered upon him: ﴿What is your business...﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 31], meaning: What is your affair? What is your story? What is the grave matter that has brought you? The word khatb (a grave matter, a serious affair) indicates a serious matter or an important event. He wanted to know what it was, and whether it concerned him or someone else.

This word also came with this meaning in His saying, in the story of our master Yusuf: ﴿He said: "What was your affair when you sought to seduce Yusuf from himself?"...﴾ [Yusuf: 51], that is: the strange matter that moved you to this act.

Our master Musa said it too when he saw the two daughters of our master Shu'ayb had come out to water the sheep: ﴿He said: "What is your business?"...﴾ [al-Qasas: 23], that is: what compelled you to come out? It seems to be an extraordinary matter, not an ordinary one. So this word is set for a grave matter that calls for astonishment and wonder.

The angels replied: ﴿They said: "Indeed, we have been sent to a people who are criminals"﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 32]. Here Ibrahim was reassured and understood that the matter did not concern him. The criminal people at this time were the people of Lut. Then they explained their mission: ﴿to send down upon them stones of clay﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 33].

It is understood that stones differ from clay. Stones have a hardness and severity that varies in strength and solidity according to the type of stone, beginning with marble, then granite, then slab-stone and limestone.

So how can stones be of clay, when the two descriptions appear contradictory? They said: it is clay that was heated in the fire until it became hard and solid, as we do, for example, in the making of pottery.

The meaning of ﴿marked by your Lord for the transgressors﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 34] is: marked (mu'allamah), each stone bearing the name of its owner and its address; it is specified for him and not for another, and directed at him, not missing him.

His saying ﴿by your Lord...﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 34] indicates that they descended from the sky and are not stones of the earth, and that they were marked by God, coming thus ready-made; our task is to pelt them with them by the names of their owners, so that no stone is mixed with another.

The meaning of ﴿for the transgressors﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 34]: the musrif (transgressor) is one who exceeds the limit in disobedience. So there are limits to matters: limits to the lawful and limits to the unlawful, which the Truthful, glorified is He, has explained, and taught us how to stop at these limits. Concerning the lawful He, exalted, said: ﴿These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229].

And concerning the unlawful He said: ﴿These are the limits of God, so do not approach them...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187]. That is: stop at the limits of the lawful and do not go beyond them to something else; as for the unlawful, beware of approaching it. Beware even of merely drawing near to it, for if you draw near it you are about to fall into it; this is a protection for you.

As He, glorified, said to Adam: ﴿And do not approach this tree...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35], and He said: ﴿And do not approach fornication...﴾ [al-Isra': 32]. Regarding the unlawful, He does not forbid us from the act alone, but forbids us from approaching its causes.

So in what did these criminal transgressors exceed the limits? They exceeded the limits in committing a forbidden act that contradicts the pure nature which God created. For when God, exalted, willed to place a khalifah (vicegerent) on earth, He created Adam and created with him his spouse so that reproduction would be accomplished, and tribes would come forth who populate the earth, for its populating does not stand on one or two persons, but requires a multitude of people.

Then He also made reproduction in everything that He wills to grow and continue, to serve this khalifah: ﴿And of everything We created pairs...﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 49].

If mankind is going to reproduce, then the area of land on which they live must grow, and the plants on which they live must multiply: He, exalted, said: ﴿And He spread from both of them many men and women...﴾ [al-Nisa': 1]. So we need cultivation proportionate to this increase.

Whoever reflects on this matter of reproduction in plants and in humans finds it according to the importance of the thing and the extent of benefit and use from it. We say, for example: when you sow radishes, you can eat from them after ten days, cucumbers after forty days, and dates after four years.

Every thing takes from you before it gives you, in proportion to its importance. If you want a human being, then undoubtedly he needs much effort and burdens. Therefore the Creator, glorified is He, linked him in the matter of reproduction to an overpowering pleasure that surpasses every other pleasure the human feels in all his limbs, surpassing the pleasure of the eye when it sees, the ear when it hears, the tongue when it tastes, the nose when it smells, and the hand when it touches, because each of the limbs has its own task and direction.

As for sexual pleasure, it pervades all the limbs. Had the Creator, glorified is He, not linked reproduction to this pleasure, no one would have approached it or borne its burdens.

You can imagine the difference between raising a child and raising a lamb or a calf, for example. The lamb stands and walks behind its mother a few minutes after birth, while the child walks after a year and a half.

Its walking comes in stages: after several months he can sit, after several more months he crawls, then stands, then walks.

Therefore we see that human childhood is the longest childhood among all creatures. Hence the Creator, glorified is He, linked the process of reproduction in humans to this overwhelming pleasure that a human cannot resist, to be an incentive for him to reproduce; otherwise he would not take upon himself this responsibility and this hardship.

From here too Islam was concerned with forming the family, and set for it of the controls what ensures its success. This instinct does not come simply as it does in animals; rather, He made for it rules for choosing a righteous wife, urged choosing the one who is religious, and made a period of betrothal so that each party may get to know the other.

It permitted each of the two to look at the other, so that each spouse may choose what suits him and pleases his taste and desire in the other sex. Then it prescribed the bridal gift (mahr) and the marriage contract, all so that the nucleus of the family would be strong and firm, prepared to receive life with all its burdens and responsibilities.

The crime these people committed, for which they deserved the punishments that befell them, is that they diverted this instinct which God placed in man from its lawful face to another, forbidden face with no benefit or fruit.

A face that contradicts sound nature and upright tastes: they would come to males instead of coming to women as God permitted. It is known that coming (ityan) is confined to the place of tilling and cultivation: ﴿So come to your tilth however you wish...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 223].

So their act was excess on their own selves, and transgression of the limit God prescribed, and coming in a place other than the proper one is equally forbidden whether it is a man coming to a man or to a woman; all of it is unlawful.

Since this act was fornication deserving stoning, God stoned them, not with stones of the earth, but with stones from the sky descending upon each one of them by name, specific to him and not to another, such that He left none of them, and annihilated them utterly, every one.

The Qur'an links the two because our master Ibrahim, at the very beginning of the matter of the call, confronted the man who argued with him about his Lord. It appears from the context of the story that he claimed divinity, as evidenced by his saying: ﴿I give life and cause death...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 258].

After that, Ibrahim had positions in showing the signs of Allah to the people; he was the first to teach them to reflect on the cosmic signs. Then came his positions with the worshippers of idols, especially with his father Azar. Then came the events of his being thrown into the fire, then he was granted a son, and was tested with the command to slaughter him, then came the story of building the House, and so on to the end of the events of his story.

The meaning is: in Musa there is a sign of Allah, conjoined to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those with certainty﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 20]. Likewise, in Musa there are signs, ﴿when We sent him to Pharaoh with a clear authority﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 38], i.e., with a clear, evident proof.

It has already been made clear that authority (sultan) may be the authority of force and subjugation that compels the opponent, or the authority of proof and argument that persuades him.

Musa (peace be upon him) possessed only the proof of persuasion, and he had no strength over Pharaoh with which to subdue him. So Allah gave him a clear authority by which to persuade Pharaoh, namely the signs and miracles that accompanied his call.

Had he challenged them with something they did not know, the challenge would have had no meaning. Therefore the miracle of our master, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), was the Qur'an, because the Arabs excelled in eloquence and fluency, so He challenged them with what they excelled in.

It is known that Pharaoh oppressed the Children of Israel because they had aided the Hyksos when they raided Egypt and cooperated with them against Pharaoh, until the Hyksos prevailed, abolished the Pharaonic system, and made it a monarchy.

So when Allah, glorified is He, wished to deliver the Children of Israel from the grip of Pharaoh, He sent Musa for this mission.

Or "with his pillar" means "with his side."

When you turn away from a person, you give him your side, then you turn your back to him after having been facing him. The Noble Qur'an depicted this matter in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah—give them tidings of a painful punishment. The sorcerer has the ability to arrange things and has the cleverness to make people see things other than as they are. The madman, on the other hand, does not arrange things and has no ability to control his desires and impulses; rather, he is the confusion of falsehood and its bankruptcy.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, took vengeance upon Pharaoh: ﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea, while he was blameworthy﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 40]. Allah seized them by placing in their souls a love of overtaking Musa, and enticed them to it until they followed them and plunged into the sea after them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 51, verse 46:

The people of Nuh as well are a sign and a lesson ﴿from before⟩ [al-Dhariyat: 46], before Pharaoh and before 'Ad and Thamud ﴿Indeed, they were a people who were defiantly disobedient⟩ [al-Dhariyat: 46], departing from the obedience of Allah and denying His Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him).

The Qur'an has elaborated their story in detail in other places, and that Nuh remained in calling them for a thousand years less fifty years, and yet only a few believed with him. They plugged their ears against his call, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and became arrogant with great arrogance, until Nuh despaired of them and invoked against them. ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except wicked disbelievers⟩ [Nuh: 26-27].

Here he summarizes their condition: ﴿Indeed, they were a people who were defiantly disobedient⟩ [al-Dhariyat: 46], meaning: departing from the obedience of Allah, from our saying: "fasaqat al-rutabah 'an qishratiha" (the ripe date fell out of its skin), i.e., it separated from it.

Al-rutab is the soft unripe date (al-balah al-layyin) which has received water, so there is moisture in it. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, made it food for Sayyidah Maryam, as He said, glorified is He: ﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates. So eat and drink and be comforted⟩ [Maryam: 25-26], meaning the rutab was for her both food and drink at once.

This is a rhetorical image depicting the Shari'ah of Allah as the membrane that protects the fruit: the Shari'ah protects the believer just as the skin protects the fruit. So beware of leaving this covering which shields you, protects you, and adorns you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 51, verses 47–49:

By "the sky" (al-sama') is meant everything that is above us. ﴿We built it with might (bi-ayd)﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 47], that is, with strength, power and wisdom, and building requires a process in which there is firmness (makin). Then He said: ﴿And the earth—We spread it out﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 48], that is, We smoothed it and spread it out.

So the sky has the quality of stability, and therefore He said ﴿We built it﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 47]. The earth's quality is change: what is elevated in it becomes lowered, and the features upon it are subject to change. Therefore He said ﴿We spread it out﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 48], and We prepared it in a state that gives comfort to its inhabitants, just as we prepare a child's bedding, so that nothing in it disturbs him.

﴿How excellent are the ones who spread out!﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 48]. It comes from the word mahd (cradle, a comfortable bed), and even a child's bedding we constantly clean and change from time to time; likewise the earth's quality is change and non-permanence.

His saying, glorified is He, ﴿And of everything We created pairs, that you may remember﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 49]. In another place the Exalted said: ﴿Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36]. This phrase, ﴿and of what they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36], has made us await a pairing that we do not yet know.

With the advance of scientific research, we have found pairing in the atom, we have found that rain is not formed except when pollination of the clouds occurs, we have recognised pairing in the electric current, and they have found it even in inanimate matter.

The scholars still have much in their quiver, all of which are matters that minds could not bear before, because the Arab nation in which the Qur'an was revealed was an unlettered nation, having nothing of culture; and had these matters been revealed to them, they might have been overwhelmed by them and turned away because of them from the essence of the call.

Therefore the Exalted gives them a concise telegram in ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53], so that the door remains open, encompassing every development and anticipating everything new.

The sin (in sa-) indicates the future, and "nurihim" (We shall show them) is a present-tense verb indicating continuity; so these discoveries remain, and their wellspring does not run dry until the Day of Resurrection.

And if the process of reproduction is in most cases and generally from a male and a female, the Exalted reserves for Himself the freedom of power, and gives us examples of human beings that came contrary to this rule.

It is as if He, glorified is He, is saying to us: Beware lest you think that I am confined to these causes; rather, I create what I will: I create from two pairs, I create without two pairs at all, and I create from a single pair.

That is: the freedom of power has encompassed all its aspects in this matter. Then ﴿and He bestows barrenness on whom He wills﴾ [al-Shura: 50], so marriage is available, but reproduction does not come.

And because the matter of the creation of all pairs is a wondrous matter, the Exalted opened it with His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him who created all the pairs﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36]; that is: do not be astonished, for you are before the power of God, and He is exalted above being measured by anything else.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 51, verses 50–51:

This is a command to flee (al-firar), and fleeing, that is running away, takes place from a dreadful thing that approaches you while you are afraid of it, and you want to save yourself from it and flee to a safe refuge that protects you. The elements of this process are the one who flees, the thing fled from, and the place fled to.

The addressees here, from God the Exalted, are His servants, and He says to them: ﴿So flee to God...﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 50]. From what do they flee?

If the fleeing is to God, then they flee from everything that contradicts God, and from everything that opposes His law. They flee from Iblis, who disputes with God regarding the obligations; they flee from the desires of their own souls; they flee to God from caprices and whims; they flee from punishment to lasting bliss.

So, the meaning of fleeing here is moving from a frightening thing to a secure thing, and you will not find for yourselves a refuge safer for you than the bosom of your Creator, glory be to Him, for in it is security, rest, happiness and bliss. Even the punishment, when He legislates it for disobedience, He legislates it so that you return to Him and flee to His court.

He, glory be to Him, is keen upon you because you are His servants and His handiwork, and every craftsman is keen upon the safety of his handiwork and its protection from what destroys it.

We, in turn, learn this lesson from our Lord, blessed and exalted be He, so we perfect our works, as our master the Messenger of God (ﷺ) taught us. The perfection of craftsmanship increases the note of faith and creed in the universe, and it is enough that everyone who sees your craftsmanship says: "God, God," so you become a cause of the remembrance of God. This note is not repeated by man alone; rather the whole universe repeats it and is delighted by it. Man is only one member of this remembering system.

So: ﴿So flee to God...﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 50]: cling to His rope, hold fast to His guidance, and be on His side; be with His law, travel with Him wherever He goes, as they say among us about the peasants (hang on to your Lord and put your foot down as you wish). For as long as you are at God's side, nothing will harm you. And the poet was right:

O Lord, Your love is in my blood and my being, a bright light melting into my conscience.

I shall not be wronged, and in Your precinct is my protection; I shall not fear, and in Your pleasure is my hope.

As for the saying of God the Exalted: ﴿Indeed I am to you from Him a clear warner﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 50], the speaker here is the Messenger of God, who is the warner from God. He said ﴿a warner﴾ because fleeing is suited to warning, so that you flee from what frightens you to what gives you security. And ﴿clear﴾ means: my warning to you is evident, and my proof is manifest and apparent.

﴿And do not set up with God another god. Indeed I am to you from Him a clear warner﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 51]. That is: do not take any god other than God, to whose command you submit. It is known that those who worshipped idols, or worshipped what is other than God the Exalted, worshipped them because they have no commands, no obligations, and no method; therefore their worship is void.

As for God the Exalted, He is the true God who deserves to be worshipped and obeyed in His commands and prohibitions. The prohibition in ﴿And do not set up with God another god...﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 51] is connected to the command in ﴿So flee to God...﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 50], since there is no god besides Him, and there is no refuge for you except Him.

This is the true religion which the sound nature has approved since we were in the stage of the atoms (dharr), when God took this covenant from us: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ [Al-A'raf: 172].

Creation deviated from this covenant only due to heedlessness, or the whispering of Satan, the incitements and the desires of souls. The disbelievers worshipped idols only to satisfy the nature of religiosity within them; they worshipped them as a form of religion, to satisfy their nature, and to feel at ease because there is no accountability to them, since they have no command and no prohibition.

Before the intelligent person proceeds to act, he should bring to mind its consequences and the recompense for it. When he approaches disobedience, he should imagine the punishment awaiting him for it; when he is lazy in obedience, he should imagine the bliss prepared for him. If people did this and considered the consequences, they would flee from disobedience to obedience.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 51, verses 52–53:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Thus⋯﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 52], meaning: just as happened to those before them, and there befell them what befell them of the descent of punishment upon them by the thunderbolt and by the barren wind. So let them await that the like of this will descend upon them, for it is not far from them. Do not grieve, for you are not the first messenger whom his people have denied. ﴿Thus, no messenger came to those before them but they said: "A sorcerer or a madman."﴾

It has already passed that they accused the messengers of Allah of sorcery and madness, so be patient. ﴿So whether We show you some of what We promise them or We take you in death, to Us they will be returned﴾ [Ghafir: 77].

That is, if the punishment does not descend upon them in this world, it awaits them in the Hereafter.

Allah has shown mercy to these deniers of His Messenger despite their disbelief and obstinacy, in honour of the presence of the Messenger of Allah among them. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ [al-Anfal: 33].

The Messenger of Allah, our master, was eager for the guidance of his people, whatever they did, and he would always privately entreat his Lord, saying: "My community, my community."

We have already explained the falsity of this accusation. The Prophet can never be a sorcerer or a madman, for these two attributes are farthest from describing the Prophet, since he is an exemplar in conduct, and you never witnessed in him any sign of sorcery or madness.

Had he been a sorcerer, he would have bewitched you, and you would have believed in him as others did. Had he been mad, he could not have arranged affairs in this manner, nor would he have conveyed to you the message of his Lord. Moreover, the accusation of sorcery contradicts the accusation of madness; how then did you combine these two attributes against him?

Therefore, after this, He says: ﴿Did they charge one another with it?⋯﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 53]. It is as if the denying nations throughout history enjoined one another with this saying: "Say of the Prophet: he is a sorcerer and a madman." It is as though there were a prior agreement among them and insistence on their part to deny the messengers and persist in contentiousness and obstinacy.

Therefore, Allah turns away from them and from their accusations and says: ﴿Rather, they are a transgressing people﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 53], meaning: leave these people alone, for they are a transgressing people, that is, those who exceed the bounds.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 51, verses 52–53:
