Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 51, verses 56–58:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56]. Creation (al-khalq) is the bringing of matter into existence from non-existence and shaping it without a prior model. Creation in this sense belongs to Allah alone. Nevertheless, He did not deprive His creatures of this attribute entirely; He gave them the attribute of creating according to their capacity.

And He, glorified, said of Himself: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14]. You are a creator when you bring into existence something new that did not exist before. For example, the one who makes a cup from sand is called a creator because he brought it into being; yes, he is a creator, and he is not deprived of the fruit of his effort.

As for the Truthful One, glorified, He is the best of creators. It is well known that humans create from existing material, whereas He, glorified, creates from what does not exist. Humans create inert matter with no life in it, whereas the Creator, glorified, creates a living creation that is continually renewed, that grows and matures, along with other aspects of this question. So we create, but Allah is the best of creators.

Furthermore, the Truthful One here specified the jinn and humankind in the matter of worship and did not mention another, greater creation, the angels. It has been said: the angels were not mentioned in this context because they were created for worship and have no choice in it. They are created for this from the outset, prepared for the worship of Allah, and disposed to it: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6].

The discussion here concerns the chosen creation, which is expected to obey and is expected to disobey. If you say: why did He place the jinn before humankind in this matter?

Some scholars said: He placed the jinn before humankind because worship is either secret or open, and the worship of the jinn is secret, since we do not see them, and secret worship is more excellent because showing off (riya') does not enter it, whereas the worship of humankind is generally open and showing off enters it.

This view can be answered: the worship of the jinn is secret with respect to us, since we do not see them, but it is open with respect to their own kind, and showing off can enter it too, for they see one another.

However, the matter may be explained in another way. We say: if you read the Qur'an attentively, you will find that the jinn were created before us: ﴿And the jinn We had created before from the fire of scorching wind﴾ [al-Hijr: 27]. So He placed them before humankind because they were created before them.

Moreover, most of humankind's turning away from worship is due to Satan, who is of the jinn: ﴿except Iblis, who was of the jinn and defied the command of his Lord...﴾ [al-Kahf: 50]. For this reason they were placed before us in the matter of worship.

The construction in His saying: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56] is a construction of restriction (qasr). That is, the creation of humankind and the jinn is restricted to worship; it is the sole purpose of this creation. He did not create them for anything other than the worship of Him, glorified.

Worship means the obedience of the worshipper to the one worshipped in His commands and prohibitions. This worship in this sense is true worship, and it is what Allah requires of the servants. Therefore Allah accepts only that which is purely for Him.

This true worship is not performed by all creatures; rather, each of them performs it according to the measure of his spirit and according to his view of the true God whom he worships.

Humans, as human beings, vary in this matter, and the highest of them in it are the messengers. The best of the messengers is the last of them, Muhammad (ﷺ). He realised worship in accordance with the will of the Truthful One, glorified, in it.

For this reason, some go to excess and say: the whole universe was created only for the sake of Muhammad (ﷺ). We say: it suffices that he (ﷺ) is the best worshipper of Allah, because worship is a meaning, and a meaning is not realised except by a true worshipper, and he is the one who fulfils what Allah wills.

This true worshipper does not come from ordinary people; rather, he comes from among the prophets, and the master of the prophets and their seal is our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He is the best who realised worship to Allah.

Therefore: the purpose of creation is worship, and Allah, exalted, is free in His acts from being subject to a cause. He does what He wills, for what He wills, in what He wills. The cause that is impermissible in His acts is a cause that would return to Him, glorified.

As for a cause that returns to others, it may be explained. Worship is not for Him, glorified, except for the benefit of all creation, because it is what makes them happy in this world and saves them in the Hereafter. Nothing from it returns to Allah, because He, glorified, is free of need from His creation; their obedience does not benefit Him and their disobedience does not harm Him.

He created the creation while possessing all the attributes of perfection, so He did not gain by this creation any attribute He did not previously have. He is a Creator before He creates, a Provider before He provides, and One glorified before there exists anything to glorify Him.

If worship, as we have said, is the obedience of the worshipper to the one worshipped in His commands, "do" and "do not do," then in this sense it encompasses the whole movement of life and is not confined to prayer, fasting and zakat, as some who separate religion from the movement of life would have it.

They say: there is no politics in religion and no religion in politics. This is a false and incorrect saying. Those who do this want to give themselves a temporal authority that submits to their desires so that they may do what they wish.

They have deliberately avoided linking themselves to the method of heaven in managing the affairs of the earth, because the heavenly method restricts their movement, and they forget that it also restricts the movement of the governed in favour of their interests.

Therefore: Allah's method encompasses the whole of life, from the summit of "There is no god but Allah" to removing harm from the road. If the matter were as they say, would we leave the murderer unpunished, leave the adulterer without applying the prescribed penalty, leave the drinker of wine, leave the corrupters to corrupt, and leave people not forbidding one another from an evil they have committed?

Therefore: what do they want by suspending the law of Allah and isolating it from the movement of life? The Truthful One made worship for the benefit of creation, organising the movement of their lives and making them happy.

And always in this matter we mention the sacred hadith: how then do we exclude the religion of Allah from the movement of our lives, when it enters even the most basic matters? Will you concern yourselves with the politics of dogs while leaving the politics of humans, whom Allah has honoured?

And there is also in the sacred hadith: [text as in the commentary], meaning: strive in the movement of life, for play is movement without benefit and without purpose, and Allah wants the movement of His servants to be beneficial and purposeful.

If you take the aspect of worship and its most important part, prayer for example, do you not need, to fulfil this duty, to cover the 'awrah? How? With garments you wear. How do these garments reach you?

Consider from the first planting of cotton until a garment reaches you to wear: it is a long journey of striving, work and exertion, in which thousands take part, serving you in this matter.

Therefore: the movement of life is not prayer alone; rather, everything that helps me perform the prayer, and everything that helps me perform zakat, fasting and hajj.

Therefore: worship is a matter that pervades the whole movement of life. How then can we separate religion from the movement of life entirely, let alone separate it from the politics of the affairs of creation and the management of their concerns?

His saying, glorified: ﴿I do not desire any provision from them, nor do I desire that they should feed Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 57].

That is: I do not desire from My creation that they provide for Me. Indeed, He, glorified, is the Provider who undertakes the provision of all creatures. How could He expect provision from them, when He provides for their believer and their unbeliever? How, when He, glorified, existed before they came into being, and possessed all attributes of perfection before He created them?

Through the inner meaning of this provision, people provide for one another: one person's provision comes through another's hand. The Truthful One, exalted, encourages the servant to give, saying: when you provide for My servant, it is as if you had provided for Me, and when you give to him, it is as if you had given to Me.

That is because He, exalted, is the One who created people and summoned them into existence, and undertook their provision. So the hand of Allah is extended to His creation through His creation. For this reason He called charity to the poor a loan, saying: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a good loan?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245].

And in the sacred hadith: good deeds fall into the hand of Allah before they fall into the hand of the servant. Had the Truthful One, exalted, willed, He could have sent down His provision to His servants directly; but He made it pass from people's hands to people's hands, so that affection, love and mutual kindness might spread among them, and mercy and freedom from arrogance might prevail. Allah wants society to be united and to cooperate.

His saying, exalted: ﴿nor do I desire that they should feed Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 57]. Here food is conjoined with provision. Why? We have already explained that provision is everything that benefits, so knowledge is provision, forbearance is provision, generosity is provision, health is provision, and so on. Thus "provision" here is provision in general, and after it He specified food because it is the most evident element of provision, by which life subsists and is sustained. They said: wine was not mentioned because it is included in food.

﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 58]. The context here emphasises this truth so as to fix it in minds, so that each of us may be reassured that his provision is guaranteed. ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider...﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 58]: he used "inna" and then the separate pronoun "huwa" (He). ﴿...Possessor of strength...﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 58], that is, the possessor of strength. This means that the Essence is one thing, and strength is something separate from it.

In another place He speaks of strength and dominance, saying: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21]. Here strength is in the Essence, so He did not say "possessor of strength," because the context is one of demonstrating dominance over those who oppose.

Therefore He said ﴿Strong﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21]; the strong is one who prevails, but other powers may combine against him and overcome him. So He said ﴿Mighty﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21], meaning: one who prevails and is never overcome. Here He said ﴿al-Matin﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 58], that is, firm in His strength, because strength may be afflicted with weakness and so diminish.

Humans create inert matter with no life in it, whereas the Creator, glorified, creates a living creation that is continually renewed, that grows and matures, along with other aspects of this question. So we create, but Allah is the best of creators.

Furthermore, the Truthful One here specified the jinn and humankind in the matter of worship and did not mention another, greater creation, the angels. It has been said: the angels were not mentioned in this context because they were created for worship and have no choice in it. They are created for this from the outset, prepared for the worship of Allah, and disposed to it: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6].

The discussion here concerns the chosen creation, which is expected to obey and is expected to disobey. If you say: why did He place the jinn before humankind in this matter?

Some scholars said: He placed the jinn before humankind because worship is either secret or open, and the worship of the jinn is secret, since we do not see them, and secret worship is more excellent because showing off (riya') does not enter it, whereas the worship of humankind is generally open and showing off enters it.

This view can be answered: the worship of the jinn is secret with respect to us, since we do not see them, but it is open with respect to their own kind, and showing off can enter it too, for they see one another.

However, the matter may be explained in another way. We say: if you read the Qur'an attentively, you will find that the jinn were created before us: ﴿And the jinn We had created before from the fire of scorching wind﴾ [al-Hijr: 27]. So He placed them before humankind because they were created before them.

Moreover, most of humankind's turning away from worship is due to Satan, who is of the jinn: ﴿except Iblis, who was of the jinn and defied the command of his Lord...﴾ [al-Kahf: 50]. For this reason they were placed before us in the matter of worship.

The construction in His saying: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56] is a construction of restriction (qasr). That is, the creation of humankind and the jinn is restricted to worship; it is the sole purpose of this creation. He did not create them for anything other than the worship of Him, glorified.

Worship means the obedience of the worshipper to the one worshipped in His commands and prohibitions. This worship in this sense is true worship, and it is what Allah requires of the servants. Therefore Allah accepts only that which is purely for Him.

This true worship is not performed by all creatures; rather, each of them performs it according to the measure of his spirit and according to his view of the true God whom he worships.

Humans, as human beings, vary in this matter, and the highest of them in it are the messengers. The best of the messengers is the last of them, Muhammad (ﷺ). He realised worship in accordance with the will of the Truthful One, glorified, in it.

For this reason, some go to excess and say: the whole universe was created only for the sake of Muhammad (ﷺ). We say: it suffices that he (ﷺ) is the best worshipper of Allah, because worship is a meaning, and a meaning is not realised except by a true worshipper, and he is the one who fulfils what Allah wills.

This true worshipper does not come from ordinary people; rather, he comes from among the prophets, and the master of the prophets and their seal is our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He is the best who realised worship to Allah.

Therefore: the purpose of creation is worship, and Allah, exalted, is free in His acts from being subject to a cause. He does what He wills, for what He wills, in what He wills. The cause that is impermissible in His acts is a cause that would return to Him, glorified.

As for a cause that returns to others, it may be explained. Worship is not for Him, glorified, except for the benefit of all creation, because it is what makes them happy in this world and saves them in the Hereafter. Nothing from it returns to Allah, because He, glorified, is free of need from His creation; their obedience does not benefit Him and their disobedience does not harm Him.

He created the creation while possessing all the attributes of perfection, so He did not gain by this creation any attribute He did not previously have. He is a Creator before He creates, a Provider before He provides, and One glorified before there exists anything to glorify Him.

If worship, as we have said, is the obedience of the worshipper to the one worshipped in His commands, "do" and "do not do," then in this sense it encompasses the whole movement of life and is not confined to prayer, fasting and zakat, as some who separate religion from the movement of life would have it.

They say: there is no politics in religion and no religion in politics. This is a false and incorrect saying. Those who do this want to give themselves a temporal authority that submits to their desires so that they may do what they wish.

They have deliberately avoided linking themselves to the method of heaven in managing the affairs of the earth, because the heavenly method restricts their movement, and they forget that it also restricts the movement of the governed in favour of their interests.

Therefore: Allah's method encompasses the whole of life, from the summit of "There is no god but Allah" to removing harm from the road. If the matter were as they say, would we leave the murderer unpunished, leave the adulterer without applying the prescribed penalty, leave the drinker of wine, leave the corrupters to corrupt, and leave people not forbidding one another from an evil they have committed?

Therefore: what do they want by suspending the law of Allah and isolating it from the movement of life? The Truthful One made worship for the benefit of creation, organising the movement of their lives and making them happy.

And always in this matter we mention the sacred hadith: how then do we exclude the religion of Allah from the movement of our lives, when it enters even the most basic matters? Will you concern yourselves with the politics of dogs while leaving the politics of humans, whom Allah has honoured?

And there is also in the sacred hadith: [text as in the commentary], meaning: strive in the movement of life, for play is movement without benefit and without purpose, and Allah wants the movement of His servants to be beneficial and purposeful.

If you take the aspect of worship and its most important part, prayer for example, do you not need, to fulfil this duty, to cover the 'awrah? How? With garments you wear. How do these garments reach you?

Consider from the first planting of cotton until a garment reaches you to wear: it is a long journey of striving, work and exertion, in which thousands take part, serving you in this matter.

Therefore: the movement of life is not prayer alone; rather, everything that helps me perform the prayer, and everything that helps me perform zakat, fasting and hajj.

Therefore: worship is a matter that pervades the whole movement of life. How then can we separate religion from the movement of life entirely, let alone separate it from the politics of the affairs of creation and the management of their concerns?

His saying, glorified: ﴿I do not desire any provision from them, nor do I desire that they should feed Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 57].

That is: I do not desire from My creation that they provide for Me. Indeed, He, glorified, is the Provider who undertakes the provision of all creatures. How could He expect provision from them, when He provides for their believer and their unbeliever? How, when He, glorified, existed before they came into being, and possessed all attributes of perfection before He created them?

Through the inner meaning of this provision, people provide for one another: one person's provision comes through another's hand. The Truthful One, exalted, encourages the servant to give, saying: when you provide for My servant, it is as if you had provided for Me, and when you give to him, it is as if you had given to Me.

That is because He, exalted, is the One who created people and summoned them into existence, and undertook their provision. So the hand of Allah is extended to His creation through His creation. For this reason He called charity to the poor a loan, saying: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a good loan?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245].

And in the sacred hadith: good deeds fall into the hand of Allah before they fall into the hand of the servant. Had the Truthful One, exalted, willed, He could have sent down His provision to His servants directly; but He made it pass from people's hands to people's hands, so that affection, love and mutual kindness might spread among them, and mercy and freedom from arrogance might prevail. Allah wants society to be united and to cooperate.

His saying, exalted: ﴿nor do I desire that they should feed Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 57]. Here food is conjoined with provision. Why? We have already explained that provision is everything that benefits, so knowledge is provision, forbearance is provision, generosity is provision, health is provision, and so on. Thus "provision" here is provision in general, and after it He specified food because it is the most evident element of provision, by which life subsists and is sustained. They said: wine was not mentioned because it is included in food.

﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 58]. The context here emphasises this truth so as to fix it in minds, so that each of us may be reassured that his provision is guaranteed. ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider...﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 58]: he used "inna" and then the separate pronoun "huwa" (He). ﴿...Possessor of strength...﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 58], that is, the possessor of strength. This means that the Essence is one thing, and strength is something separate from it.

In another place He speaks of strength and dominance, saying: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21]. Here strength is in the Essence, so He did not say "possessor of strength," because the context is one of demonstrating dominance over those who oppose.

Therefore He said ﴿Strong﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21]; the strong is one who prevails, but other powers may combine against him and overcome him. So He said ﴿Mighty﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21], meaning: one who prevails and is never overcome. Here He said ﴿al-Matin﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 58], that is, firm in His strength, because strength may be afflicted with weakness and so diminish.

Among the Qur'an's methods is that it mentions opposites. After speaking of the believers, it speaks of the Makkan disbelievers, who are the intended ones in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, for those who wronged, there is a portion like the portion of their companions⁠﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 59]. They wronged through their denial and obstinacy toward the Messenger of Allah and their standing against the call, so they deserved that there be for them ﴿a portion like the portion of their companions⁠﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 59], meaning: a share of punishment like the share of their counterparts among the deniers of earlier nations, 'Ad, Thamud and Pharaoh.

The dhanub (bucket-share, a word for a bucket) is the bucket with which water is drawn out of the well, and the rope tied to the bucket is called the rishaʾ (rope). If the water is abundant, the bucket comes up heavy and slow. Therefore they said:

"The buckets that are slowest to overflow are those that fill most, and the clouds that move most heavily are those that are fullest."

The Arab poet expresses this meaning when he says:

"When a man praises another for his gift, and lengthens the praise, he has lengthened his satire."

"If the water's depth was not measured at the drawing-point, he would not have lengthened his rope."

For the depth of the water in the well calls for a long rope; likewise, the distance of the gift from the one praised calls for a long praise.

So: drawing water with a bucket was an Arab custom, and although the dhanub is poured for them so that they may drink in this world, here the dhanub will pour punishment upon them in a pouring.

As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Boiling water will be poured over their heads⁠﴾ [al-Hajj: 19]. It is poured upon the deniers from Quraysh, just as it was poured upon the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud and the people of Pharaoh, for disbelief is one creed across the ages.

Therefore, when the Truthful, glorified is He, spoke of the punishment of the people of Lot, He said: ﴿And We rained upon it stones of hard clay, layered, marked from your Lord. And it is not far from the wrongdoers⁠﴾ [Hud: 82-83]. So the punishment that descended upon the earlier peoples is not far from the later ones.

Here He emphasized this meaning, saying: ﴿So let them not ask Me to hasten⁠﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 59], because it will certainly befall them and is not far from them; it is merely a matter of a time and an appointed hour awaiting them.

The word "wayl" (ويل): they said it is a valley in Hell, and they said it means "woe." That is: destruction, punishment, and a curse from God upon those who have departed from His obedience and have not fulfilled the purpose for which they were created, which is the worship of God alone.

When they became independent of God, God became independent of them. He removed them from His mercy and made them abide eternally in His punishment. He will not decree their death so that they die, nor will He lighten their punishment.

Therefore God related about them: ﴿They will call out, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us." He will say, "Indeed, you will remain."﴾ [43:77] And He said about them: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment...﴾ [4:56]

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿the Day they are promised﴾ [51:60], it means their day which God promised them and warned them of. God did not seize them unawares, nor leave them in heedlessness; rather, He made the consequences clear to them. So He said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it...﴾ [41:46]
